name: PageHeader
purpose: Introduces a page or major section: title, optional supporting description, and trailing actions in one consistent row.
neverUseFor: Card or panel titles — use Card's own header slot instead
Breadcrumbs or wayfinding — PageHeader is the destination, not the trail
Repeated inside a scrollable list — PageHeader is a page-level element, used once per view
rationale: PageHeader gives every view the same title, description and trailing-actions row so pages are predictable to scan (2.4.6 Headings and Labels). It's the destination, not the trail, and is used once per view — card titles and breadcrumbs are separate concerns.

mayExtendLocally: Write the title and description per page
Put any Helix Buttons/IconButtons in the actions slot
mustEscalateToDS: Adding breadcrumbs, tabs or new regions into PageHeader
Changing the title type scale or spacing tokens
Using PageHeader inside Cards or repeated in lists

anatomy.description: Layout wrapper — title/description on one side, actions on the other.
The page or section title. Heading level set by the `level` prop.
Supporting one-line description below the title.

props.name: label
props.description: The page or section title text.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting one-line description shown below the title.

props.name: level
props.description: Heading level of the title — 1 for a page, 2 for a major in-page section. Never skip a level to change visual size; that's what CSS is for.

props.name: actions
props.description: Trailing content — typically a Button and/or Badge.

a11y.role: banner (implicit only when PageHeader is the page's single top-level heading region — not applied automatically)

focus.note: focus is drawn by Button — see their a11y.applied.focus

motion: CSS transitions/animations: neutralised by the global prefers-reduced-motion rule

properties.name: level
properties.description: 1 = h1, Heading / 2xl / Bold · 2 = h2, Heading / xl / Bold.

properties.name: description
properties.description: Show/hide part: the line carries its own 4px top (spacing/2xs), so hiding it changes nothing else.

properties.name: actions
properties.description: Shows the actions slot (a primary Button instance as a placeholder; 8px gap — the slot can mix groups, e.g. Badge + Button).
